description: E2E Training Benchmark - Compare youmu_page_aligned vs lerobot end-to-end training throughput on Qwen3-VL-2B with batch size sweep until OOM

userStories.title: Create benchmark job YAML configs
userStories.description: As a developer, I want per-batch-size YAML configs for both backends so that I can run each configuration as a separate training job.
acceptanceCriteria: Base YAML at configs/multimodal/qwen3_vl/qwen3_vl_libero_bench.yaml with: model_path /home/ubuntu/huggingface/Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct, obs_len=4, pred_len=2, max_steps=50, use_wandb=false, flash_attention_2, rmpad_with_pos_ids=true
Script scripts/generate_bench_yamls.py generates YAML variants for each (backend, micro_batch_size) combo: backends=[youmu_page_aligned, lerobot], micro_batch_sizes=[1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64]
Generated YAMLs saved to configs/multimodal/qwen3_vl/bench/ with names like bench_page_aligned_bs1.yaml, bench_lerobot_bs4.yaml

Each YAML sets: libero_dataset_backend, micro_batch_size, global_batch_size = micro_batch_size (single GPU), output_dir = /tmp/bench_<backend>_bs<N>, libero_data_dir = /home/ubuntu/dataset/hf_vla_64k for youmu_page_aligned or /home/ubuntu/dataset/hf_vla for lerobot
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Base the YAML on configs/multimodal/qwen3_vl/qwen3_vl_libero.yaml but change: model_path to /home/ubuntu/huggingface/Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct, libero_data_dir to /home/ubuntu/dataset/hf_vla_64k, output_dir to /tmp/bench_*, data_parallel_mode to fsdp2 (needed for single GPU too), init_device to meta. Keep: attn_implementation flash_attention_2, rmpad_with_pos_ids true, freeze_vit false, max_seq_len 2048. The generate script should read the base YAML, modify fields, and write variants.

userStories.title: Write e2e training benchmark script
userStories.description: As a developer, I want a script that runs training jobs across all configs and collects timing metrics, so that I can compare backends automatically.
acceptanceCriteria: New script scripts/benchmark_e2e_training.py that iterates over generated YAML configs in configs/multimodal/qwen3_vl/bench/
For each config: launches training via torchrun --nproc_per_node=1 tasks/omni/train_qwen_vl_libero.py --config <yaml>, captures stdout/stderr
Extracts timing: steps/sec (from training output or wall clock / steps), samples/sec (steps/sec * micro_batch_size), total wall-clock time for 50 steps
Captures peak GPU memory via nvidia-smi or torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated after each run
If run OOMs (non-zero exit or 'CUDA out of memory' in output), logs OOM and skips larger batch sizes for that backend
Saves results to benchmarks/e2e_training_results.csv with columns: backend, micro_batch_size, steps_per_sec, samples_per_sec, wall_clock_sec, peak_gpu_mem_mb, status
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Training command: torchrun --nproc_per_node=1 tasks/omni/train_qwen_vl_libero.py --config configs/multimodal/qwen3_vl/bench/<yaml>. Parse training output for per-step timing — look for patterns like 'step X/50' or throughput logging. Exclude first 10 steps as warmup, measure steps 10-50 (40 steps) for stable timing. Run backends in ascending batch size order; stop when OOM. Clean up /tmp/bench_* output dirs between runs to avoid disk pressure. GPU: single H100 80GB.

userStories.title: Run the full e2e training benchmark
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to run the benchmark to completion and collect results for both backends across all viable batch sizes.
acceptanceCriteria: Run scripts/benchmark_e2e_training.py to completion
Results CSV contains data for both backends across at least 4 batch sizes each
OOM boundary identified for each backend (largest successful batch size recorded)
Results saved to benchmarks/e2e_training_results.csv
userStories.notes: This will take a while — 50 steps per config, up to 14 configs (7 batch sizes × 2 backends). Expect ~2-5 min per config. Run in tmux. Some large batch sizes will OOM quickly. Total runtime estimate: 30-60 minutes.

userStories.title: Write benchmark report
userStories.description: As a developer, I want a report summarizing the e2e training throughput comparison so that the impact of page-aligned data loading on real training is clear.
acceptanceCriteria: Report at benchmarks/e2e_training_benchmark_report.md
Table: steps/sec, samples/sec, wall-clock time, peak GPU memory per (backend, batch_size)
Analysis: at which batch sizes does data loading become the bottleneck vs GPU compute
Analysis: maximum batch size before OOM for each backend
Analysis: peak GPU memory comparison between backends
Conclusion: overall training speedup (or lack thereof) from page-aligned data loading
userStories.notes: Expected pattern: at small batch sizes (bs=1,2), data loading dominates and page-aligned should show clear speedup. At large batch sizes (bs=16+), GPU compute dominates and both backends should converge to similar steps/sec. The crossover point reveals when data loading optimization stops mattering. If both backends OOM at the same batch size, GPU memory usage is model-dominated (not data-dominated).
